messages.content: You are a precise biomedical information extraction assistant. Follow the requested output format exactly and never add explanations.

Given the following text and a relational triplet extracted from it:

Text: The most important interactions with spironolactone are medicines that also raise potassium.
The combined effect of these medicines can push your potassium level dangerously high.
Tell your doctor about every medicine you take, including anything you start or stop during treatment.
Be especially careful with:
eplerenone, which should not be taken with spironolactone at all;
medicines that raise potassium, including ACE inhibitors such as lisinopril and ramipril, ARBs such as losartan and valsartan, NSAIDs, heparin and low molecular weight heparin, and trimethoprim;
potassium supplements and potassium-containing salt substitutes, which are usually stopped when spironolactone is started for heart failure;
Spironolactone slows how fast your kidneys clear spironolactone.
Spironolactone can cause lithium toxicity.
Lithium levels need monitoring.
Digoxin needs care for two separate reasons.
Spironolactone interferes with one type of blood test used to measure digoxin.
Spironolactone can raise the actual amount of digoxin in your body.
Triplet: ["spironolactone", "interferes with", "blood test used to measure digoxin"]

The relation 'interferes with' in the triplet is defined as 'The subject drug may affect or disrupt the accuracy or function of the test or process specified by the object entity.' In this context, is there any relation appropriate to replace it? Choose a relation whose meaning and subject/object direction match the triplet even if the wording differs; choose 'None of the above' only if no candidate fits. Please answer by providing only the letter of your choice.

Choices:
A. 'causes false positive results in': The subject substance may lead to incorrect positive results in the test or assay specified by the object entity.
B. 'has side effect': The subject drug may cause the adverse effect or symptom specified by the object entity.
C. 'interacts with': The subject drug has a drug interaction with the drug or substance specified by the object entity that may change effects or cause harm.
D. 'not same as': The subject drug's effect is not the same as the event or condition specified by the object entity.
E. 'has interaction effect': The subject drug, when interacting with other substances, may cause the specific effect or outcome described by the object entity.
